story.titleZh: 奥迪巴库带来14项气动升级，比诺托称符合预期
story.summaryZh: 奥迪在阿塞拜疆大奖赛前为巴库带来14类气动升级件，领队比诺托表示数据第一印象显示套件符合预期。一练仅博尔托莱托使用新套件，二练两车分列第14、15位。
story.originalTitle: 'The package is delivering as expected' – Audi reflect on new upgrade package after practice ahead of 2026 Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix
story.summaryEn: Audi brought 14 aerodynamic upgrade components to Baku ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with Team Principal Mattia Binotto saying the first impression from the data is that the package is delivering as expected. Only Gabriel Bortoleto ran the new package in FP1, and the two cars finished P14 and P15 in FP2.
detailZh: “套件正按预期交付”——奥迪在阿塞拜疆站练习后谈新升级套件。奥迪为争取本赛季进一步提升性能，在巴库带来了14个新部件。
奥迪领队马蒂亚·比诺托认为，车队在阿塞拜疆大奖赛前引入的重大升级套件“正按预期交付”。
这支欣维尔车队在FIA周末前提交的气动升级清单上勾选了14个类别，其中包括大幅改动的前翼和后翼、修订版地板以及新的引擎盖布局等。
作为相关性验证流程的一部分，一练中只有加布里埃尔·博尔托莱托使用了升级件，从而可以在巴库与尼科·霍肯伯格驾驶的旧规格赛车进行直接对比。
“如果看数据的第一印象，可以说，这套件正按预期交付，”比诺托说。
“这是好事，事实上这也是我们本周末的主要关注点。对我们来说，升级当然对性能很重要，对我们在锦标赛中的竞争也很重要。
“但同样，对我们来说，更重要的是确保车队在方法论和能力方面持续发展。
奥迪在巴库带来大量升级。“因此，从心态上的勇敢，到我们可能交付的气动概念类型，再到交期、工程、生产、制造，我们把挑战提上去了。
“就我们在这里带来的升级而言，最终能带来多少圈速提升并不重要。
“我认为对我们最重要的是，我们提高了挑战，再次在心态和交期等方面推动了整个系统，并希望我们能与风洞和模拟器保持正确的相关性。”
奥迪目前位列车队积分榜第八，仅落后哈斯4分，霍肯伯格和博尔托莱托在最近六场大奖赛中合计五次进入积分区。
博尔托莱托使用新套件在一练中位列第10，紧随其后的是霍肯伯格，随后两人在第二节练习中分列第14和第15。
“我觉得赛车在二练中感觉并不好，”博尔托莱托说。
“说实话，我们缺一点抓地力，还不明白原因。我对此没有答案。
“我猜这就是巴库，低附着、灰尘很大。赛道我想已经好几年没清理过了，我们只能这样开，然后尽力而为。”

detailEn: 'The package is delivering as expected' – Audi reflect on new upgrade package after practice in AzerbaijanAudi have brought 14 new components to Baku in a bid to gain further performance this season.
Audi Team Principal Mattia Binotto believes the team's major upgrade package, which has been introduced ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, is "delivering as expected".

The Hinwil outfit ticked 14 category boxes on the FIA’s pre-weekend submission list of aerodynamic upgrades, which includes substantially changed front and rear wings, a revised floor, and a new engine cover arrangement amongst others.
As part of the correlation process, only Gabriel Bortoleto had the updates in FP1, allowing for a direct comparison with Nico Hulkenberg’s older spec car in Baku.
“If you look at the first, let me say, impression of the data, the package is delivering as expected,” said Binotto.
“Which is good, which is our main focus, as a matter of fact, for the weekend. For us, upgrading, yes, it’s important for the performance, it’s important for our fight in the championship.
“But again, for us, what’s more important is to make sure that the team is developing in terms of methodologies and capacity.

Audi have a big raft of upgrades in Baku"So from being brave when it comes to mindset, to the type of aero concepts we may deliver, on the lead times, engineering, production, manufacturing, we raised the challenge.
"With the upgrade we have brought here, it doesn’t matter how much it will deliver in terms of lap time.

"I think what matters for us the most is having raised the challenge, having again pushed the system on whatever is mindset and lead times, and hopefully we’ll have a correlation which is right compared to the wind tunnel and the sim.”
Audi sit eighth in the teams' standings, just four points behind Haas, with Hulkenberg and Bortoleto having finished in the points at five of the last six Grands Prix between them.
Bortoleto was able to finish P10 in FP1 with the new package, just ahead of Hulkenberg, before the pair finished P14 and P15 in the second session.
“I think the car didn't feel amazing in FP2,” said Bortoleto.
“If I'm very honest, we're lacking a little bit of grip, still to understand why. I don't have answers for that.
“I guess that's Baku, low grip, super dusty. The track has not been cleaned, I think, for a few years now, and yeah, just we need to drive with this and then try our best.”

relatedItems.titleZh: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛二练：拉塞尔领跑安东内利与维斯塔潘
relatedItems.summaryZh: 在阿塞拜疆大奖赛周四二练中，梅赛德斯车手拉塞尔以1分43.347秒的最快圈速占据榜首，队友安东内利和红牛的维斯塔潘分列二、三位。
relatedItems.originalTitle: FP2: Russell leads Antonelli and Verstappen in second Azerbaijan GP practice
relatedItems.summaryEn: George Russell topped the second practice session at the Baku City Circuit with a 1:43.347, completing a Thursday practice sweep. His Mercedes team mate Kimi Antonelli was second, 0.552 seconds behind, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen third.
detailZh:
二练：拉塞尔领跑安东内利和维斯塔潘，阿塞拜疆大奖赛第二节练习赛
乔治·拉塞尔在巴库城市赛道实现了周四练习赛的全场完胜，他在第一节和第二节自由练习中均名列成绩榜首位。
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛周四的第二节练习赛中，乔治·拉塞尔轻松占据榜首，领先梅赛德斯队友基米·安东内利和红牛的马克斯·维斯塔潘。
拉塞尔通过连续多圈使用倍耐力软胎，做出了1分43.347秒的最快圈速，比车手积分榜领跑者安东内利快了半秒，比维斯塔潘又快了三 十分之一秒（十分之三秒）。
当地时间1600，维修区尽头的绿灯亮起时，大量赛车迅速驶上赛道——夕阳渐渐落在巴库城市赛道上空，但气温仍然高达30摄氏度，相当炎热。
大部分车手在本节练习的前期阶段使用中性胎或硬胎，维斯塔潘早早做出 1分45.115秒 的基准圈速，但他随即通过无线电抱怨自己的红牛赛车行驶感受很差。
“我的后轴不断离地，所以我一直在反向打方向修正，”这位四届世界冠军几分钟后强调道，随后他用中性胎把成绩提升到 1分44.492秒——比使用同款轮胎的梅赛德斯车手拉塞尔快了百分之几秒。
FORMULA 1 QATAR AIRWAYS AZERBAIJAN GRAND PRIX 2026
名次 车手 圈速 1 拉塞尔 RUS 1:43.347 2 安东内利 ANT +0.552秒 3 维斯塔潘 VER +0.827秒 4 勒克莱尔 LEC +1.126秒 5 汉密尔顿 HAM +1.318秒
再往后一点，兰多·诺里斯排在了第三位，领先于刘易斯·汉密尔顿、回归的伊萨克·哈贾尔、夏尔·勒克莱尔以及队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，两辆迈凯伦赛车针对第一节自由练习中的地板问题采用了临时解决方案——用塑料扎带固定。
随后，在本节练习进行到将近20分钟时，赛会出示了红旗，原因是阿尔维德·林德布拉德在8号与9号弯之间的城堡路段推得太狠，撞上了护墙并停下，他的小红牛赛车右侧受到了严重损坏。
“我真的很抱歉，”这位英国新秀在无线电里说道，上一站马德里的第二节自由练习中他也曾发生撞车。“我觉得我真的就差了大概一毫米就蹭到了，”他补充道，随后他被医疗车接走并送回了围场。
在林德布拉德的赛车被回收、赛道清理完毕后，本节练习于当地时间16点29分恢复——大家的注意力现在转向了用软胎进行的排位赛风格模拟，以及首次观察本周末单圈速度的竞争格局可能如何展开。
然而，各节练习与排位刚刚恢复，比尔曼和哈斯车队就遭遇了戏剧性一幕。“我的引擎关掉了，然后就……坏了，”比尔曼叹息道。他还是设法把车停在了缓冲区末端，给救援人员减轻了工作负担。
林德布拉德连续第二个大奖赛周末在第二次自由练习中撞车退出。当比尔曼和林德布拉德在场边观看时，其他车手开始用软胎刷出成绩——拉塞尔做出1分43.759秒领跑，领先维斯塔潘约四 十分之一秒（0.4秒），勒克莱尔、汉密尔顿和安东内利则落后接近一秒。
又一轮计时后，拉塞尔跑出1分43.347秒，随后队友安东内利也大幅提升成绩，以1分43.899秒升至第二。此时维斯塔潘被挤到第三，后面依次是勒克莱尔、汉密尔顿和诺里斯（后者放弃了更有力的一圈）。
加斯利驾驶他的阿尔派赛车名列第七，排在他前面的是皮亚斯特里、哈贾尔以及哈斯仅剩的奥康，之后是队友科拉平托、小红牛的劳森——他在最后一个计时段被慢速行驶的汉密尔顿挡住而懊恼不已——以及凯迪拉克的佩雷斯。
博托莱托和霍肯伯格分别排在第14和第15位，奥迪继续通过大量升级件进行学习，压过了同样进行了升级的威廉姆斯车队阿隆索——不对，是阿尔本和塞恩斯的赛车，以及林德布拉德、博塔斯驾驶的另一辆凯迪拉克、比尔曼以及阿斯顿·马丁的赛车——其中阿隆索的里程因疑似漏油而受到限制。
随着第一节和第二节自由练习结束，各车队和车手将在围场重新集结，连夜分析数据，然后于周五当地时间12点30分回到赛道，开始最后一小时练习赛。

detailEn: FP2: Russell leads Antonelli and Verstappen in second Azerbaijan GP practiceGeorge Russell made it a Thursday practice clean sweep at the Baku City Circuit, having topped the times in both FP1 and FP2.

George Russell comfortably set the pace during Thursday’s second practice session ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, leading the way from Mercedes team mate Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen.

Russell worked his way down to a time of 1m 43.347s with a series of runs on Pirelli’s soft compound tyre, putting him half a second up on championship leader Antonelli, and a further three tenths clear of Verstappen.

Plenty of cars were quick to head out on track when the green light switched on at the end of the pit lane at 1600 local time – the sun gradually setting over the Baku City Circuit, but the air temperature still sitting at a toasty 30 degrees Celcius.

Most drivers spent the early stages of the session running either medium or hard tyres, bringing an early benchmark of 1m 45.115s from Verstappen, who nonetheless promptly got on the radio to complain about a poor ride at the wheel of his Red Bull.

“I’m constantly counter-steering because my rear axle is coming off the ground,” stressed the four-time World Champion a few minutes later, before improving to a 1m 44.492s on medium tyres – a few hundredths faster than Mercedes’ George Russell with the same compound.
FORMULA 1 QATAR AIRWAYS AZERBAIJAN GRAND PRIX 2026
Pos.DriverTime1George RussellRUS1:43.3472Kimi AntonelliANT+0.552s3Max VerstappenVER+0.827s4Charles LeclercLEC+1.126s5Lewis HamiltonHAM+1.318s

A little further back, Lando Norris slotted into third over Lewis Hamilton, the returning Isack Hadjar, Charles Leclerc and team mate Oscar Piastri, with the two McLarens running a makeshift solution to their FP1 floorboard issues in the form of plastic cable ties.

Then, just under 20 minutes into the session, a red flag was thrown due to Arvid Lindblad pushing too hard through the Turn 8/9 castle section, thumping the wall and coming to a halt with significant damage on the right-hand side of his Racing Bulls car.

“I’m really sorry,” said the British rookie over the radio, having also crashed during FP2 in Madrid last time out. “I think I literally clipped it by like a millimetre,” he added, before being collected by the Medical Car and dropped off in the paddock.

With Lindblad’s car recovered and the track cleared, the session resumed at 1629 local time – attention now turning towards Qualifying-style simulations on soft tyres, and a first look at how the one-lap pecking order might unfold this weekend.

Only moments after the session had resumed, though, there was drama for Ollie Bearman and Haas. “My engine switched off and just… broke,” sighed Bearman, who managed to park his car at the end of an escape road and make the marshals’ job easier.

Lindblad crashed out of FP2 for the second successive Grand Prix weekendAs Bearman and Lindblad watched from the sidelines, the rest of the field started to deliver some soft-shod times – Russell pumping in a 1m 43.759s to lead Verstappen by some four tenths, and Leclerc, Hamilton and Kimi Antonelli the best part of a second adrift.

Another round of runs brought a 1m 43.347s from Russell, before team mate Antonelli delivered his own significant improvement to go second on a 1m 43.899s. Verstappen was shuffled down to third at this point, from Leclerc, Hamilton and Norris (who backed out of a stronger lap).

Pierre Gasly put his Alpine seventh, ahead of Piastri, Hadjar and the sole remaining Haas of Esteban Ocon, followed by team mate Franco Colapinto, Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson – frustrated by a slow-moving Hamilton in the final sector – and Cadillac’s Sergio Perez.

Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg were 14th and 15th respectively as Audi continued to learn about a raft of updates, over the similarly upgraded Williams cars of Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz, Lindblad, the other Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas, Bearman and the Aston Martins – Fernando Alonso’s running limited by a suspected oil leak.

With FP1 and FP2 completed, the teams and drivers will now regroup in the paddock and dig through the data overnight before returning to the track for the final hour of practice, which is set to begin at 1230 local time on Friday.

detailZh: 利亚姆·劳森：“我不明白”为什么阿尔维德·林德布拉德在撞坏我的底板后没有受到处罚
小红牛两名车手之间的碰撞，差点毁掉了车队原本意外取得的不错成绩
阿尔维德·林德布拉德，小红牛，利亚姆·劳森，小红牛
利亚姆·劳森表示，他“不明白”阿塞拜疆大奖赛的赛事干事为何没有对小红牛队友阿尔维德·林德布拉德采取进一步行动，后者在今天的F1比赛中把他撞得原地打转。
在亚历山大·阿尔本于巴库第30圈撞车退赛并引发安全车出动后，劳森和林德布拉德在比赛重启前分列第12位和第14位。
绿旗挥出后，弗兰科·科拉平托严重锁死车轮，把阿尔平队友加斯利和兰多·诺里斯都撞出了比赛。与此同时，林德布拉德比身前的劳森和埃斯特班·奥康刹车更晚，最终被夹在两车之间，并把队友的车撞得打转。
赛事干事认为这次碰撞是由于“林德布拉德可用的空间有限，以及前方事故引发的连锁反应”造成的，因此林德布拉德免于受罚——但劳森虽然在查看这次碰撞之前发表讲话，却并不完全认同这一结果。
这位新西兰车手回顾道：“进入1号弯时，我的加速出现严重迟滞，完全没有动力，所以埃斯特班就在我旁边。我试图给他留出空间，然后我左侧面被撞得非常猛，车底被撞出一个洞，之后我们就没什么办法再战斗了。我不太清楚到底发生了什么。”
“我一直尽量保持干净的驾驶，今年有些时候显然比较激进，但是……我不知道，进入1号弯时想从两辆车中间那样挤过去，我觉得本来就不太可能实现。”
利亚姆·劳森，小红牛；阿尔维德·林德布拉德，小红牛
当被问到干事的判罚对车队有利但对他本人不太有利时，劳森评论道：“对车队来说是好事。显然我不会去抗议我的队友，但是……
“我不理解这个判罚，因为我被撞得那么重，我的底板上都被撞出了一个洞。我当时只是在转向过弯，还给了对方空间。从我坐的位置来看我不理解，但可以说这对车队来说是好事。”
林德布拉德一有机会就向队友道了歉。他在媒体采访区再次表达了歉意，同时部分将这次事故归咎于埃斯特班·奥孔在刹车时移动路线——但录像画面并不支持这一说法。
这位新秀说：“从我那边的情况来看，我和埃斯特班在直道上已经这样交锋了大约三次，我们几次接近又刹车又再次加速，所以场面完全混乱，赛车的电池也因此在不太理想的工作区间。”
“然后大家在1号弯都刹车得稍微有点晚，我当时准备对埃斯特班完成超越，但他在最后一刻移动了路线，基本上就是在刹车时变线，所以我不得不采取躲避动作，这导致我的前轮轻微锁死，然后就撞上了利亚姆。”
“我在无线电上说了‘对不起’，但归根结底这不是故意的。如果你回看视频，就能看到我的动作没有任何故意成分。干事们判定‘不予进一步处罚’，我对此当然感到高兴，但说到底，我也不知道你想让我怎么做。如果我们都在极限边缘，大家都刹车得很晚，而我前面的车手在最后一秒移动了路线……当时有很多起事故。我什么也做不了，事情就是这样。”
林德布拉德补充说，小红牛告诉他：“我们看得出你其实没什么别的办法”，尽管他仍然预料到自己“会挨一点训斥”。
无论如何，对于这支总部位于法恩扎的车队来说还是有积极一面的——林德布拉德追回到第七名，以0.03秒的优势从奥康手中抢下了这个位置，而且阿尔派由于科拉平托的失误显然未能得分。这意味着在车队积分榜第五名的争夺中，理论上出现了13分的摆动，目前小红牛领先15分。
“从积极的角度看，我们作为一支车队拿到了积分。说实话，今天我们非常非常幸运，阿尔派没有得分，”劳森承认。“我们没有他们那样的速度。”
“某种意义上我们接受这个结果，因为这个周末我们挣扎了很多，这是本赛季我们第一次难以在排位赛第一节脱身，”林德布拉德表示赞同。“所以能成为除领先集团之外的最佳，并拿到大量积分，真是太棒了。这个周末并不轻松，但积分终究是在周日正赛里拿下的。”
林德布拉德本周日可能实际上拿不到任何积分，但他至少在周六把任务完成了。
detailEn: Liam Lawson: “I don’t understand” why Arvid Lindblad escaped penalty after wrecking my floor
A collision between the Racing Bulls jeopardised what turned out to be an unexpected decent result for the team
Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls
Liam Lawson says he ‘doesn’t understand’ Azerbaijan Grand Prix stewards took no further action against Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who spun him around in today’s Formula 1 race.
After Alexander Albon crashed out on lap 30 in Baku, causing a safety car intervention, Lawson and Lindblad lay 12th and 14th ahead of the restart.

When the green flag was waved, Franco Colapinto had a massive lock-up and took both Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. Meanwhile, Lindblad braked later than Lawson and Esteban Ocon ahead of him, ending up sandwiched between the two cars, and sent the sister car into a spin.

The stewards deemed the collision to have been caused by “the restricted space available to [Lindblad] and the chain reaction caused by the incident ahead”, hence Lindblad escaping a penalty – but Lawson, albeit speaking before reviewing the clash, didn’t quite agree with that outcome.

“Coming into Turn 1, I had massive boost lag and I didn’t have any power, so Esteban was next to me,” the New Zealander recounted. “I tried to give him space and then I just got hit from my left so hard that it put a hole on the floor, and we couldn’t really fight after that. I don’t really know what happened.

“I’ve always tried to keep clear, and it’s been obviously aggressive at points this year, but… I don't know, going into Turn 1 there to try and fit through the middle of two cars like that, I don't think it was ever really going to happen.”
Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls
Asked if the stewards’ decision was good for the team but not so much for him, Lawson commented: “Great for the team. Obviously I'm not going to go and protest my team-mate, but…

“I don't understand it, because I got hit so hard that it put a hole in my floor. I was just turning for the corner, giving the guy space. From where I'm sitting I don't understand, but let's say it's great for the team.”

Lindblad did apologise to his team-mate as soon as he got the opportunity to. He reiterated this in the media pen while partly blaming the incident on Esteban Ocon moving under braking – which the footage doesn’t corroborate.

“From where we were, me and Esteban, we'd gone about three times on the straight, we'd sort of gone and braked and gone again, so it was complete chaos, the battery wasn't in a good window because of that,” the rookie said.

“And then everyone braked a little bit too late in Turn 1, and I was going to make the move on Esteban and he moved in the last minute, basically moved under braking, so I had to take avoiding action, which meant I locked the front slightly and I hit Liam.

“I said ‘I'm sorry’ on the radio, but in the end it's not intentional. If you watch the video back you can see there's nothing intentional about what I do. The stewards said ‘no further action’, which obviously I'm happy about, but in the end, I don't know what you want me to do. If we're all on the limit, we all brake very late, and the guy in front of me moves in the last second… There were many incidents. There was nothing I could do, and it is what it is.”
Lindblad added that Racing Bulls told him, ‘We can see there's not much you could have done’, though he did expect to “get a little bit told off” still.

Regardless, there were silver linings for the Faenza-based outfit – Lindblad recovered to seventh, snatching that position away from Ocon by 0.03s, and Alpine obviously failed to score following Colapinto’s blunder. That represents a theoretical 13-point swing in their battle for fifth in the constructors’ championship, with Racing Bulls now 15 points ahead.
“On the positive, we scored points as a team. We got very, very lucky today that Alpine didn’t, honestly,” Lawson admitted. “We didn't have [their] speed.”

“We take the result, in a sense, because we've struggled a lot this weekend, it's been one of the first times this season we've struggled to get out of Q1,” Lindblad concurred. “So to be best of the rest and scoring massive points is absolutely amazing. It's not been an easy weekend, but points are scored on Sunday.”
Lindblad may not actually score any points this Sunday, but he did get the job done on Saturday after all.
